transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because... I just don’t care about anything anymore. It’s like all the things I used to do, I just can't be bothered. Not my art classes, or board-game nights, or hiking... I was even supposed to be getting back to the soccer team, but... I don't know. Now I just sit in my room while everything just kind of slips away. 

Which is a shame because I used to really love those game nights. My friend Jessica used to host them on Thursdays, and she always made this amazing cheese dip in this tiny little slow cooker she found at a garage sale. It had these painted orange daisies on the side of it. She collects a lot of vintage kitchen stuff, actually, her whole apartment looks like it's stuck in the 1970s. She even has one of those rotary phones on the wall, though I don't think it actually works. I keep meaning to ask her where she finds all that stuff, but... yeah. I just stay in my room now.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

Yeah... most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It just sits there. It feels like there’s no future for me beyond the apartment walls. I stare at those walls a lot, actually. They have this weird textured wallpaper that looks kind of like oatmeal. I tried to peel a little piece off in the corner by the baseboard once, but it’s glued on there really tight. The landlord said it was installed in the nineties by the previous owners, who apparently had a bunch of cats. I’m actually allergic to cats, which is why I never got one, even though Jessica keeps telling me a pet would be good for me. She has a pug named Barnaby who snores louder than a person. He has this little plaid sweater he wears in the winter when she takes him for walks... but anyway, yeah. Just that heavy feeling.
Do you still enjoy the things you used to love, even if you don't feel like doing them?

No, I... I really don't. Like I was saying before, I just don't care about any of it anymore. The art classes, the hiking, the game nights... it's all just... nothing to me now. I don't even care about the soccer team, which is wild because I played for three years. We had these bright blue jerseys that always got grass stains on the elbows no matter how much you bleached them. I tried soaking mine in this special eco-friendly detergent once, but it just made it smell like pine needles. My mom used to use pine cleaner on our kitchen floors when I was a kid. She'd mop every Saturday morning while listening to ABBA on this old cassette player. The tape deck would always jam on "Dancing Queen," and she'd have to pull the tape out with a pencil... but no, I don't enjoy anything. I just sit in my room and watch it all slip away.
Do you feel any pleasure at all when you do manage to engage in these activities?

No, there's no pleasure. Like I said, I just don't care about anything anymore. It's not just that I don't feel like doing them, it's that when I try, or even think about trying, it's all just... flat. The art classes, the game nights, the hiking... even the soccer team. I just sit in my room while everything slips away. 

I used to have my art supplies set up by the window in my room. It's a nice window, actually, it gets the morning sun. But the glass has this tiny crack in the bottom corner. The landlord said a bird flew into it before I moved in. I always wondered what kind of bird it was. Maybe a robin? We used to have robins in our yard when I was little. They'd pull worms right out of the grass after it rained. The smell of rain on pavement always reminds me of that house. We had a driveway that was so steep, my dad's car used to scrape the bottom every time he pulled in... but yeah. No pleasure. I just sit in my room.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been a long time. I think it became constant around the following summer, so... maybe a year and four months now? That summer was really hot. I remember the air conditioner in my apartment broke right in the middle of July. The repair guy took three days to come out, and he was this older man who kept complaining about his knees. He said he needed surgery but couldn't afford the time off work. He had this big toolbox that was covered in stickers from different national parks. I've never been to a national park, actually. I always wanted to go to Yosemite. I saw a documentary about it once on public television. The narrator had this incredibly soothing voice, kind of like Morgan Freeman, but not him. I think I fell asleep watching it, which is weird because I usually have so much trouble sleeping. But yeah, about a year and four months of just... feeling like this.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?

Well, it really depends on the day. Sometimes making coffee feels like I'm lifting wet cement. Every movement is just... dragging. The coffee maker I have is this old drip machine I bought at a garage sale. It's an awful shade of yellow, like mustard that's been left out in the sun too long. The lady who sold it to me had these huge plastic earrings shaped like parrots. They clacked against her jaw when she talked. She told me she was moving to Florida to live with her sister who breeds miniature poodles. I always thought poodles were kind of high-maintenance dogs, with all the grooming they need. My neighbor used to have a standard poodle that would bark at the mailman every single day right at 11:00 AM. Our mailman was this really tall guy who always wore shorts, even in December when it was snowing... but anyway. Yeah, sometimes I'm just so slow. But then other days, I just pace. I'll walk from the kitchen to the window over and over until my legs actually ache.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?

Yeah, I've lost weight. My jeans have gotten so loose lately that I actually have to knot the waistband just to keep them up. I just... I go most of the day without eating because food just tastes like cardboard to me now. Even my favorite foods. I used to make this really good baked ziti. My grandmother taught me how to make the sauce from scratch. She had this enormous cast-iron pot that she brought over from Italy, and it weighed an absolute ton. I don't know how she lifted it, honestly, because she was only about four foot eleven. She used to wear these thick woolen sweaters, even in the summer, because she said her blood was thin. She kept peppermint candies in the pockets, the kind with the red and white swirls wrapped in that clear cellophane that crinkles really loudly. I tried to find those exact candies at the grocery store last week, but the aisle was being restocked by this teenager who was listening to music so loud I could hear the bass through his headphones. It was some kind of electronic dance music, I think. But anyway, yeah, I don't really eat much anymore.
Do you often find yourself pacing back and forth in your room?

Well, I think I mentioned this just a bit ago, but yeah, I do. It's either one extreme or the other, honestly. Some days I'll just pace, like, back and forth from the kitchen to the window, over and over until my legs actually ache. The floorboards by the window squeak a little. It's an older building, you know? The landlord said it was built in the 1920s, back when they used real hardwood. He's this guy who always wears these faded polo shirts with the collars popped up, like he's stuck in an 80s movie or something. He drives this bright red convertible that he parks right in front of the building, taking up two spaces. My neighbor, the one who used to have the poodle, left a really angry note on his windshield once. She wrote it in pink glitter pen, which I thought was a funny choice for an angry note. I used to love those glitter pens when I was in middle school. We'd write notes to each other and fold them into little triangles. I had this one friend, Sarah, who could fold them so perfectly they looked like origami. She ended up moving to Seattle in the eighth grade because her dad got a job at Boeing. I always wondered if it rains as much there as people say. But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, the pacing. Yeah, I pace a lot on the days I'm not moving so slowly that, like I said, making coffee feels like I'm trying to lift wet cement.
Have you ever thought about harming yourself or wished you were dead?

Yeah... I have. It's just... I keep having these thoughts that I just don't want to wake up anymore. It's like this heavy blanket over everything. My friend actually came over the other day and found me just sitting there, and I guess I had been saying out loud that I couldn't keep living like this. She got really scared. She's known me since we were in college. We took this art history class together, and the professor was this eccentric guy who always wore bow ties. He had a different bow tie for every day of the week, and on Fridays he'd wear one with little cartoon dinosaurs on it. He said his grandson picked it out for him. His grandson was named Oliver, I think, or maybe Leo. It was one of those names that got really popular a few years ago. I remember reading an article about how baby names go in cycles, like how all the vintage names from the 1920s are coming back now. My great-aunt was named Pearl, and she collected ceramic thimbles from all over the world. She had a whole display case for them in her hallway, right next to this grandfather clock that chimed so loudly it would make you jump if you weren't expecting it. But yeah, my friend found me and I was just saying I couldn't do it anymore. I just want to go to sleep and not wake up.
Do you usually feel like you're moving slowly or is it more that some days you're slow and others you're pacing back and forth?

I think I kind of just said this, but yeah, it really depends on the day. It's like I'm stuck between two extremes. Some days I just pace from the kitchen to the window, over and over again, until my legs literally ache. The linoleum in the kitchen is starting to peel up at the corners, actually. It's this awful mustard yellow color that I think was probably really trendy in the seventies. My mom had a kitchen that exact same color when I was growing up, complete with the matching appliances. She had this blender that was so loud you couldn't hear yourself think when she made smoothies. She used to put wheat germ in them, which gave them this really gritty texture. I could never drink them, but my brother loved them. He lives in Denver now, working as a graphic designer. He designed the logo for this local brewery out there, the one with the mountain goat on it. I've never been to Denver, but I hear the altitude can really mess with you if you're not used to it. But anyway, yeah, other times, I move so slowly that just trying to make a cup of coffee feels like I'm trying to lift wet cement. It's just exhausting.
Is the pacing or the slow movement more frequent for you overall?

Honestly, it's hard to say which one happens more. I feel like I'm just always bouncing between them. Like I was saying, some days I'm just pacing, kitchen to the window, over and over until my legs are just throbbing. And then other days, I'm so slow, like trying to make coffee is like lifting wet cement. I actually bought this new coffee a few weeks ago, a dark roast from that little shop on the corner. The barista there has this really intricate tattoo of a compass on his forearm. He told me it took three sessions to finish. I've always thought about getting a tattoo, maybe a small bird or something on my ankle, but I'm terrified of needles. When I was a kid, I had to get blood drawn, and I actually passed out right there in the chair. The nurse had to give me a juice box and a sticker, like I was five years old. It was one of those scratch-and-sniff stickers, grape scented. I used to collect those in a binder. I had pages and pages of them. But um, yeah, the pacing and the slowness... they just kind of take turns ruining my week. I don't really keep track of which one wins.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight, such as more than 5% of your body weight, over the past year?

Yeah, I guess I have. I mean, I go most of the day without eating anything at all because everything just tastes like cardboard lately. It's like there's no flavor left in the world. And my jeans have gotten so loose I actually have to knot the waistband to keep them up. I was trying to find a belt the other day, and I dug through my closet and found this old braided leather one I bought at a flea market years ago. It was one of those huge outdoor markets where people sell everything from antique furniture to homemade jam. I bought a jar of strawberry rhubarb jam from this older woman who was wearing a bright purple sun hat. She told me the rhubarb came from her own garden. She had this massive garden, she said, with tomatoes and zucchini and these huge sunflowers that grew taller than her fence. I tried to grow sunflowers once, but the squirrels kept digging up the seeds before they could even sprout. Squirrels are so persistent, you know? They just keep coming back. But yeah, the weight thing... I just don't have any interest in food right now.
Have you had any days in the past month where you felt somewhat interested in the things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. Not even a little bit. I mean, I'm basically here because I just don't care about anything anymore. Not my art classes, not the board-game nights I used to go to, not even hiking or trying to get back on my soccer team. I used to play midfield, mostly. Our jerseys were this really bright neon green color. We ordered them online from this custom sports apparel place, and when they arrived, the box smelled strongly of vinegar for some reason. The delivery guy who dropped it off was always wearing shorts, even in the middle of winter when it was snowing. I never understood how people can do that. It makes me cold just looking at them. I bought this huge, fluffy winter coat last year on sale, the kind that makes you look like a marshmallow, but it's so warm. It has these deep pockets that are perfect for keeping your hands warm if you forget your gloves. I lose gloves all the time. I'll take one off to answer my phone and then just leave it on a bench or something. But yeah... I just sit in my room now, and it feels like everything is just slipping away. I don't even care enough to try and stop it.
Have you experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that aren't your own?

Yeah, I do. It's... it's a woman's voice. She's always in the corner of my room, just telling me that I ruined everything and that I should just stay inside. And it's not like a thought, you know? It sounds as clear as if someone is standing right next to my bed. My bed actually used to be against the other wall, but I moved it last spring because the morning sun was hitting my face too early. I bought these blackout curtains to help with that, they're this deep navy blue color. I found them at a thrift store, and the lady at the register told me they originally came from a hotel that was being renovated downtown. That hotel used to have this incredible rooftop restaurant. I went there once for a friend's birthday party, and they served these little appetizers on silver trays. One of them was this goat cheese and fig tartlet, and I tried to recreate it at home once, but I burnt the pastry crust completely black. My smoke alarm went off and it took me twenty minutes to get it to stop beeping. I had to stand on a kitchen chair and wave a towel at it. But um, yeah, the voice is just... she's just always there, telling me to stay inside.
Do you experience any other unusual perceptions or hear voices when you're alone, aside from the woman's voice you mentioned?

No, it's really just her. Just that one woman's voice. She's always over there in the corner, you know, just repeating that I ruined everything and that I need to stay inside. And like I said, it's so loud and clear, exactly like she's standing right next to my bed. I actually got a new comforter for that bed a few months ago because the old one was starting to get these weird little pills all over the fabric. It was supposed to be 100% cotton, but I think it was a blend because it got so scratchy. I ordered the new one online, and the delivery driver left it on my porch while it was raining. The box got completely soaked, but luckily the comforter was wrapped in plastic inside. It's this really nice sage green color, which is supposed to be calming, right? I read somewhere that green is the most restful color for the human eye. My aunt used to have her entire kitchen painted sage green, even the cabinets. She collected these vintage ceramic roosters and had them lined up all along the tops of the cabinets. I always thought they were going to fall off if someone slammed a door too hard. But yeah, no other voices or anything like that. Just her, always telling me to stay inside.
Do you usually find it hard to get out of bed in the morning due to feeling slowed down?

Yeah, getting out of bed is... it's really hard. Some days I just, I move so slowly that even just making coffee feels like I'm trying to lift wet cement. It takes forever. I actually broke my favorite coffee mug last week because my hands just felt so heavy and clumsy. It was this mug I got from a pottery class I took a few years ago. The glaze on it was this beautiful speckled blue, like a robin's egg. I tried to glue it back together with this superglue I found in the junk drawer, but the glue had totally dried out. That drawer is a mess, honestly. It's full of old batteries and takeout menus from places that probably aren't even open anymore. There's this one menu from a Thai place that used to make the best Pad See Ew. They always gave you an extra spring roll if you ordered on a Tuesday. I don't know why Tuesday, maybe it was their slowest day. But yeah, other days it's the complete opposite. I can't stay still at all. I'll just pace back and forth, from the kitchen to the window, over and over until my legs actually ache. I just wear a path in the rug.
Have you had any moments in the past few weeks where you felt even slightly interested in doing something you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, that's kind of why I'm here, I guess. I just... I don't care about anything anymore. Nothing. I used to do all these things, like my art classes, and I'd go to board-game nights with people, or go hiking... I even played on a recreational soccer team. But now I just sit in my room while everything slips away. I haven't touched my art supplies in months. I have this set of really nice watercolor pencils that my brother got me for Christmas two years ago. They come in this tin case that has a picture of a bridge on the front. I think it's a bridge in London, maybe? Or somewhere in Europe. My brother actually went to Europe for his honeymoon. They went to Italy and ate all this amazing pasta. He brought me back a little glass turtle from Venice. It sits on my windowsill, but it gets super dusty because I never open the window anymore. The dust just sort of collects there. I tried dusting it with a paper towel once, but it just smeared the dust around and made it look worse. You're supposed to use a microfiber cloth for that kind of thing, but I don't have one. I keep meaning to buy one, but... yeah, I just don't have the energy or the interest to do anything, not even the things I used to love.
Have you experienced any other hallucinations or delusions besides the woman's voice you mentioned?

Well, I know it sounds impossible, but... I'm sure the people downstairs and some of my ex's friends have been tracking when I leave. It's because the hallway lights blink right after I think about going to the store. Like, the exact second I decide I need to go get something, they flicker. I was thinking about going to get more of that peppermint tea I like. It's the only kind that doesn't make my stomach hurt. I used to drink chamomile, but then I read this article about how some chamomile tea has high levels of lead in it, which is terrifying if you think about it. Lead poisoning can cause all sorts of neurological issues. My grandfather actually had lead paint in his old house, and he had to hire this special crew to come in and scrape it all off the walls. They wore these white hazmat suits that looked like they were going to the moon. He had this beautiful old Victorian house with a wrap-around porch. We used to sit out there in the summer and eat watermelon. He always salted his watermelon, which I thought was so weird, but he swore it made it taste sweeter. He had this salt shaker shaped like a little lighthouse. But yeah, the lights in the hallway, they definitely blink when I'm about to leave, so they have to be tracking me.
Do you often see things that aren't there, like shadows or movements out of the corner of your eye?

No, I don't really see shadows or anything like that. But I do hear that woman's voice. I mentioned her before, right? It's always coming from the corner of my room, and she just tells me that I ruined everything and that I should just stay inside. It's not like a thought in my head, it sounds exactly like someone is standing right next to my bed, just as clear as day. My bed is pushed up against the wall right now because I dropped my phone down the crack between the mattress and the headboard last month, and I had to move the whole thing to get it out. My phone case is this sparkly purple color, but the sparkles are starting to flake off. I found one of the little glitter pieces stuck to my forehead the other day. I looked ridiculous. I bought that case at a kiosk in the mall. Do you remember when malls used to be packed with people? Now they're just full of empty storefronts and those weird massage chairs that cost two dollars for five minutes. I sat in one once and it just kind of pummeled my lower back in a way that actually hurt. I think the rollers were broken. But yeah, her voice is so clear, just telling me to stay inside.
Have you experienced any other hallucinations or unusual perceptions besides the voice you've mentioned?

No, it's just her. Just that woman's voice. I know I already told you about her, but she's the only one. She just stays in the corner of my room and tells me I ruined everything, that I just need to stay inside. And it's not like a thought, you know? It's like she's right there, as clear as if someone was standing right next to my bed. My bed actually needs a new comforter. The one I have is getting all bunched up inside the cover. It's a duvet, I guess. I bought it at Target years ago when they had that really good home goods section before they remodeled the store near my apartment. Now the layout makes no sense. You have to walk all the way past the groceries to get to the pharmacy, which is just silly if you just need to pick up a prescription. I used to get my prescriptions at a local place, this mom-and-pop pharmacy, but they closed down during the pandemic. A lot of places did. It's sad, really. The owner was this nice older man who always gave out those little strawberry candies with the wrappers that look like actual strawberries. I love those. But yeah, no other voices or anything, just her telling me to stay inside.
